title: Nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence in tau-lepton pairs from electron--positron collisions
authors: Yoav Afik, Juan Ramón Muñoz de Nova, Sarthak Sharma, Surya Sundar Raman
abstract: Quantum correlations have recently attracted significant attention in collider physics, with Nonlocal Advantage of Quantum Coherence (NAQC) representing the strongest form of quantum correlation studied so far. Owing to its strength, NAQC is considerably more challenging to observe than Bell nonlocality since it is only present in narrower regions of phase space. Unlike other systems, tau-lepton pair ($τ^+τ^-$) production in electron--positron ($e^+e^-$) collisions provides an ideal testing ground, as it exhibits strong quantum correlations and, in particular, NAQC over a large region of phase space. In this paper, we investigate NAQC in $e^+e^- \to τ^+τ^-$ production at center-of-mass energies of 10.58 and 91.19~GeV, corresponding to the ongoing Belle~II and future FCC-$ee$ experiments, respectively. Remarkably, for our experimental proposal, we develop a dedicated NAQC witness, which allows to certify NAQC presence by measuring one single magnitude. We estimate the experimental sensitivities needed to establish the presence of NAQC, finding that a large fraction of the number of events (specifically, 0.18 for Belle~II and 0.31 for FCC-$ee$) contribute to the NAQC signal. A 5$σ$ observation of NAQC requires a precision of approximately 1\% at Belle~II, while a precision of a few percent is sufficient at FCC-$ee$. The resulting observation would constitute the strongest form of quantum correlation measured in a collider to date. In addition, we design an experimental scheme to implement the steering game leading to the NAQC definition, representing the first implementation of a steering game in a high-energy collider. Our results are easily extendable to other electron--positron colliders with different center-of-mass energies.
summary: This paper analyzes the Nonlocal Advantage of Quantum Coherence (NAQC) in $	au$-lepton pair production from $e^+e^-$ collisions. The authors derive a specific, measurable witness for NAQC and calculate the experimental precision needed at future colliders like FCC-ee to observe this correlation. This work represents a significant theoretical step in testing the strongest known quantum correlations in particle physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the Nonlocal Advantage of Quantum Coherence (NAQC), a strong form of quantum correlation, in particle collider physics.
main_result: The authors develop a dedicated NAQC witness and estimate the experimental precision required at Belle II and FCC-ee to observe this correlation, which would be the strongest measured in a collider to date.
method: The methodology involves deriving spin density matrices for $	au^+	au^-$ production and applying theoretical measures of coherence, such as the NAQC witness derived from a steering game.
model_or_system: The system is $	au$-lepton pair ($	au^+	au^-$) production resulting from electron--positron ($e^+e^-$) collisions at specific center-of-mass energies (10.58 GeV and 91.19 GeV). The analysis models this as a bipartite quantum system.
key_observables: NAQC witness ($W_{NA}(ho)$), spin correlation matrix elements ($C_{ij}$), and polarization vectors ($B_{i}$).
important_parameters: Center-of-mass energies (10.58 GeV, 91.19 GeV), $	au$-lepton mass ($m_	au$), and electroweak parameters ($\sin^2 	heta_W$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations in different kinematic regimes (e.g., QED dominance or ultrarelativistic limit) and assumes the helicity basis is not deformed during boosts.
figures_summary: References are made to Figure 2, which illustrates the NAQC bands in the relevant phase space.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for NAQC, derives the spin density matrix elements using weak interaction couplings, and then applies this formalism to calculate the required observables for the specified $e^+e^-$ collision energies.
why_interesting: While focused on high-energy physics, the rigorous development of a measurable quantum correlation witness (NAQC) and the implementation of a 'steering game' concept in a high-energy collider setting provide advanced theoretical tools applicable to characterizing quantum correlations in complex, multi-particle systems.
